target.body:
# PR2/5 — runtime foundation/core + terminal immutability guard

## Context capsule

This PR is item 2 of the rebuilt beta3 durable core stack. It asks reviewers to evaluate the runtime foundation/core + terminal immutability guard slice on its own base while recognizing that later PRs build cumulatively on top.

## Durable core stack overview

- PR1/5 — docs/RFC/boundary anchor and proof plan.
- PR2/5 — runtime foundation/core plus terminal SQLite row immutability guard.
- PR3/5 — wake targets, durable producers, replay/resume semantics.
- PR4/5 — controls/inspection plus CLI/Gateway surface.
- PR5/5 — internal session delivery handoff, final hardening, and cumulative E proof.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR2/5
- Current PR summary: Durable store/runtime foundation, session/task primitives, gateway/CLI protocol foundation, terminal SQLite row immutability guard.
- Does not claim: No wake-target/replay controls/internal handoff; no plugin SDK DTS size fix.
- Dependency/base: `5d9fb965cada2083c532c68cc9b95fb0f4f7d7a2` (PR1 public submitted head, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104246)
- Downstream dependency: PR3 depends on this PR
- Canonical upstream gate(s): PR1 has ClawSweeper threshold met (`platinum hermit`) and awaits maintainer decision; PR2 was rebased and verified after syncing PR1 private branch.
- This PR head: `codex/openclaw-durable-beta3-newstack-pr2-runtime-core` at `2e4129630ac2e90fe6fe66236d8e1309795d3827`
- Intended base: `5d9fb965cada2083c532c68cc9b95fb0f4f7d7a2`

## Dependency / promotion gate

- Submit/merge gate: PR2 should only be promoted after its base is canonical and threshold-met.
- Current gate state: PR1 reviewer threshold met; PR2 exact-head ancestry and local proof pass after rebase.
- Next dependent PR: PR3 depends on this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Durable store/runtime foundation, session/task primitives, gateway/CLI protocol foundation, terminal SQLite row immutability guard. This narrows review to the intended durable-runtime layer, keeps the cumulative stack ancestry clean, and gives reviewers exact-head evidence instead of relying on stale or downstream proof.

## Scope

- Durable store/runtime foundation, session/task primitives, gateway/CLI protocol foundation, terminal SQLite row immutability guard.
- Exact-head local status captured in `new-pr2-build-status.md` and refreshed by the PR2 promotion status artifact.
- Branch/head/base captured in `new-5pr-stack-final-audit.md`.

## Non-scope

- No wake-target/replay controls/internal handoff; no plugin SDK DTS size fix.
- No wake-target/replay controls/internal handoff is part of this slice.
- No plugin SDK DTS size fix is included in the durable behavior narrative.

## Base / diff hygiene

- Base comparison: `5d9fb965cada2083c532c68cc9b95fb0f4f7d7a2..2e4129630ac2e90fe6fe66236d8e1309795d3827`
- Non-cumulative check: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 5d9fb965cada2083c532c68cc9b95fb0f4f7d7a2 codex/openclaw-durable-beta3-newstack-pr2-runtime-core` passed after PR2 rebase.
- Conflict/replay notes: PR2 rebased cleanly from old PR1 head `8681317a9ec25fd14bf2253eb77c4d8abba3a41a` onto current PR1 head `5d9fb965cada2083c532c68cc9b95fb0f4f7d7a2`; intentional scope exclusions documented in status artifacts.

## Proof matrix

| Gate | Command / artifact | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Unit / focused behavior | exact-head rerun after rebase | passed locally on `2e4129630ac2e90fe6fe66236d8e1309795d3827` |
| Typecheck / static | `pnpm tsgo:core` and docs map check | passed |
| Diff hygiene | `git diff --check 5d9fb965cada2083c532c68cc9b95fb0f4f7d7a2..HEAD` and ancestry check | passed |
| Upgrade/schema, if applicable | status artifact and generated schema diffs | applicable for runtime/schema PRs; docs-only for PR1 |
| Live proof, if applicable | status artifact | not run in final audit; add before promotion if required |

## Live proof

- Environment: local worktree only for this promotion pass.
- Result: Remote/Testbox proof was not rerun; existing status artifact records earlier crabbox sanity blocker. Local exact-head focused proof passed after rebase. Runtime live proof should be added before final merge if required.
- Artifact(s): `new-pr2-build-status.md`, `new-5pr-stack-final-audit.md`, PR2 promotion status artifact.

## ClawSweeper requirements

- Includes authored `What Problem This Solves` section: yes.
- Includes authored `Evidence`/proof content: yes.
- Names stored data model / migration impact when schema or persisted state changes: yes; durable state/schema impact is covered in status artifact.
- Names risk labels ClawSweeper should evaluate: compatibility, session-state, message-delivery, durable-runtime, diff-hygiene.
- Keeps proof artifacts accessible in body or durable stack state.

## Risk / upgrade notes

- Runtime risk: durable runtime/session behavior changes require exact-head and live proof before promotion.
- Compatibility/upgrade risk: schema/runtime compatibility must be reviewed against generated state schema and status artifact evidence.
- Rollback/feature-flag posture: stack is cumulative; rollback should revert/promote by PR boundary rather than cherry-picking descendants.

## Evidence

- Focused durable/unit/commands/gateway/protocol/agents tests passed locally after rebase:
  - durable unit: 16 files, 68 tests
  - durable command: 1 file, 7 tests
  - gateway bundle: 12 files, 863 tests
  - gateway protocol: 1 file, 51 tests
  - agent/session adjacent shards: 11 files, 431 tests
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm docs:map:gen --check` passed.
- `git diff --check 5d9fb965cada2083c532c68cc9b95fb0f4f7d7a2..HEAD` passed.
- Scope exclusion grep found no `src/durable/wake-*`, `src/durable/wake-controls-inspection*`, `src/durable/wake-internal-delivery*`, or `scripts/write-plugin-sdk-entry-dts.ts` paths.
- Final ancestry audit passed for `5d9fb965cada2083c532c68cc9b95fb0f4f7d7a2` -> `codex/openclaw-durable-beta3-newstack-pr2-runtime-core` at `2e4129630ac2e90fe6fe66236d8e1309795d3827`.

## Next gate

Review this PR after PR1; PR3 remains private until PR2 reaches the configured reviewer threshold.

target.title: fix(tavily): forward abort signal when web search runs are canceled
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two cancellations bugs in the Tavily web search path:

1. **Dropped abort signal** — Tavily is one of the web search providers that discards the caller's `AbortSignal`. The web search runtime threads `signal` into `execute(args, { signal })`, but the Tavily provider ignored it — so aborted runs left Tavily requests open until their configured timeout.

2. **Fallback after cancellation** — Even after forwarding the signal, an aborted Tavily request caught by `runWebSearch`'s catch block can start the next auto-detected provider. Canceling one provider should not trigger unintended fallback work.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Tavily signal forwarding** (provider + client): Forward `context?.signal` through the Tavily provider and client to `postTrustedWebToolsJson` (which already supports `signal?: AbortSignal` at line 141). The pattern matches the searxng fix in #104216 and the DuckDuckGo fix in #104899 — one provider per PR, no new SDK surface.

**Shared runtime abort guard** (`src/web-search/runtime.ts`): Add `params.signal?.throwIfAborted()` at the top of the provider loop and `params.signal?.aborted` in the catch block so a parent cancellation stops fallback immediately. This is the canonical pattern from #104216 — without it, forwarding the signal into a provider that then rejects on abort would still trigger the next auto-detected provider.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — abort through the guarded-fetch stack

A real stalled HTTP server (never sends headers) exercises the exact code path Tavily uses:
- Production: `postTrustedWebToolsJson({ signal })` → `withTrustedWebToolsEndpoint` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetch()`
- Proof: `withSelfHostedWebToolsEndpoint` — same `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetch()` code path; only the SSRF policy differs (selfHosted allows localhost for proof).

```
[proof] Signal propagated in 122ms through guarded-fetch stack
        (withSelfHostedWebToolsEndpoint → fetchWithSsrFGuard → buildTimeoutAbortSignal → fetch)
[proof] stalled server: http://127.0.0.1:44061/stall
[proof] abort: controller.abort("proof: cancellation") @ ~100ms
[proof] error: DOMException: This operation was aborted
```

Proof script: `extensions/tavily/proof/abort-guarded-fetch-proof.test.ts`

### Signal chain — full path (source verified)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 475 | `params.signal?.throwIfAborted()` — terminal guard (new) |
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 489 | `definition.execute(params.args, { signal: params.signal })` |
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 503 | `params.signal?.aborted \|\| !allowFallback` — catch guard (new) |
| Tavily provider tool | `extensions/tavily/src/tavily-search-provider.ts` | 28 | `signal: context?.signal` (new) |
| Tavily POST helper | `extensions/tavily/src/tavily-client.ts` | 90 | `signal: params.signal` (new) |
| Trusted POST endpoint | `src/agents/tools/web-search-provider-common.ts` | 150 | `signal: params.signal` — native support |

No new SDK surface is needed — `postTrustedWebToolsJson` already accepts `signal?: AbortSignal` at line 141.

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/tavily/ src/web-search/runtime.test.ts
 ✓ tavily tools: 15/15 passed (including signal forwarding test)
 ✓ tavily client: 5/5 passed
 ✓ runtime: 31/31 passed (including "does not fall back after parent cancellation")
```

### Lint

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs \
    extensions/tavily/src/tavily-search-provider.ts \
    extensions/tavily/src/tavily-client.ts \
    extensions/tavily/src/tavily-tools.test.ts \
    src/web-search/runtime.ts \
    src/web-search/runtime.test.ts
✓ clean
```

### Landing order

The `src/web-search/runtime.ts` abort guard is included here so this PR typechecks and tests standalone. #104216 (SearXNG, same author) and #104899 (DuckDuckGo, same author) also add the same guard. Whichever lands first, the others will rebase; no cross-repo dependency.

target.title: fix(duckduckgo): forward abort signal when web search runs are canceled
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two cancellations bugs in the DuckDuckGo web search path:

1. **Dropped abort signal** — DuckDuckGo is the only web search provider that discards the caller's `AbortSignal`. While every other provider forwards `context?.signal` to its HTTP client, DDG drops it at the provider boundary. A canceled run leaves the DDG request open until its 20-second timeout expires.

2. **Fallback after cancellation** — Even after forwarding the signal, an aborted DDG request is caught by the shared `runWebSearch` catch block, which can start the next auto-detected provider. Canceling one provider should not trigger unintended fallback work.

## Why This Change Was Made

**DDG signal forwarding** (provider + client): Forward `context?.signal` through the DDG provider and client to `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint`, matching the pattern every other web search provider already uses (tavily #104965, searxng #104216, brave, exa, firecrawl, etc.). The entire chain already supports `signal?: AbortSignal` — DDG was simply the last provider not using it.

**Shared runtime abort guard** (`src/web-search/runtime.ts`): Add `params.signal?.throwIfAborted()` at the top of the provider loop and `params.signal?.aborted` in the catch block so a parent cancellation stops fallback immediately. This is the canonical pattern from #104216 — without it, forwarding the signal into a provider that then rejects on abort would still trigger the next auto-detected provider.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — abort through the guarded-fetch stack

A real stalled HTTP server (never sends headers) exercises the exact code path DDG uses: `withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetch()`. Both `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` (DDG's actual call) and `withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint` (used in this proof to allow localhost) share identical `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ signal })` → `fetch()` code paths; the only difference is the SSRF policy object.

```
        (withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint → fetchWithSsrFGuard → buildTimeoutAbortSignal → fetch)
[proof] stalled server: http://127.0.0.1:33563/stall
[proof] abort: controller.abort("proof: cancellation") @ ~100ms
[proof] error: DOMException: This operation was aborted
```

A held-open TCP connection is cancelled promptly (123ms) when the signal fires, rather than waiting for the configured 20-second timeout.

Proof script: `extensions/duckduckgo/proof/abort-guarded-fetch-proof.test.ts`

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |

| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 475 | `params.signal?.throwIfAborted()` — terminal guard (new) |
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 489 | `definition.execute(params.args, { signal: params.signal })` |
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 503 | `params.signal?.aborted \|\| !allowFallback` — catch guard (new) |
| DDG provider tool | `extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-search-provider.ts` | 53 | `signal: context?.signal` (new) |
| DDG client | `extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-client.ts` | 201 | `signal: params.signal` (new) |
| Trusted endpoint wrapper | `src/agents/tools/web-search-provider-common.ts` | 105 | `signal: params.signal` → `withTrustedWebToolsEndpoint` |
| Guarded fetch router | `src/agents/tools/web-guarded-fetch.ts` | 88 | Spread `...params` → `withWebToolsNetworkGuard` |
| SSRF guard | `src/infra/net/fetch-guard.ts` | 496-498 | `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ signal: params.signal })` |

No new SDK surface is needed — the entire chain already accepts `AbortSignal`.

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/duckduckgo/ src/web-search/runtime.test.ts
 ✓ DDG: 12/12 passed (including signal forwarding test)

```

### Lint

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs \
    extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-search-provider.ts \
    extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-client.ts \
    extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-search-provider.test.ts \
    src/web-search/runtime.ts \
    src/web-search/runtime.test.ts
✓ clean
```

The `src/web-search/runtime.ts` abort guard is included here so this PR typechecks and tests standalone. #104216 (SearXNG, same author) also adds the same guard. Whichever PR lands first, the other will rebase; no cross-repo dependency.

target.title: fix(synology-chat): bound outbound NAS response bodies to prevent Gateway OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Synology Chat outbound calls would unbounded-buffer the NAS HTTP response body into Gateway memory when the chatbot webhook or `user_list` endpoint streamed a large or stuck reply.

Inbound Synology webhooks were already capped (`readRequestBodyWithLimit`, #25831). Outbound `doPost` / `fetchChatUsers` still used `data += chunk` with no byte limit (and `doPost` discarded the body after only checking status).

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `readRequestBodyWithLimit` from the plugin SDK on both outbound paths:

- chatbot POST responses: **64 KiB** discard budget (status-only)
- `user_list` GET responses: **1 MiB** parse budget (legacy name → user_id)

Oversized chatbot responses fail closed without burning the send retry budget. Oversized `user_list` responses warn and fall back to cache, matching existing error semantics.

Proof script stays local (`.local/`, gitignored) so the PR stays small (2 files).

## User Impact

Operators running Synology Chat are protected from Gateway memory blow-ups when a NAS (or mis-pointed `incomingUrl`) returns an oversized outbound response. Normal small webhook / user-list replies are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Scope:** 2 files, +154 / -41

**Unit tests:**

